Exclusions: listwise deletion of rows missing any model variable (3 of 351 rows excluded; n=348 used; observation unit = one quadrat visit; properties recur across rounds but quadrats do not). rows.note: OUTCOME: Binary occurrence of any Eucalyptus seedling in the quadrat (euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m > 0); 90/348 (25.9%) positive. EXPOSURE: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover alone (percent of quadrat), single untransformed class, chosen after both the all-grass sum and the exotic-grass sum were excluded; annual exotic grasses are the dominant grass layer in these grazed remnant woodlands and the growth form most implicated in competitive suppression of seedling establishment; good contrast (mean 12.4%, range 0-76, 46 zero quadrats). MODEL: GLM y ~ ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + Euc_canopy_cover + Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m) + C(Season), family=Binomial(logit), property-cluster-robust SEs (18 clusters). FOCAL ESTIMATE (native log-odds scale): -0.00725 per +1 percentage point of exotic annual grass cover, SE 0.01110; t = -0.653 with small-sample df = 17 (clusters-1), p = 0.52; OR = 0.993, 95% CI (0.970, 1.016). EXCLUSIONS: 3 rows dropped listwise for missing cover/canopy/distance values; n = 348 of 351; no missing seedling counts. INFERENCE: No statistically detectable effect; point estimate slightly negative (more grass, weakly less recruitment). Estimate sign consistent across all four specifications run in this trajectory (all-grass on 0-50cm count: -0.01234 SE 0.01031; exotic sum on count: -0.00617 SE 0.01923; exotic sum on presence: -0.01435 SE 0.00977; exotic annual on presence: -0.00725 SE 0.01110), none significant; the combined exotic-grass presence specification carried the strongest signal, suggesting the perennial exotic component drives most of the weak association. Per-property spatial covariates (climate/soil/radiation) intentionally omitted as collinear with the property cluster absorbed by cluster-robust SEs. Script: scripts/annualgrass_logit.py.
rows.predictor: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover (percent of quadrat covered by exotic annual grass, single class, no transformation); effect reported per +1 percentage point on the log-odds of seedling presence

Estimate is essentially null with slight negative sign: grass cover shows no detectable effect on seedling recruitment. rows.predictor: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover (percent ground cover of exotic annual grasses in the quadrat, raw single-column measure, untransformed; coefficient is log rate-ratio in expected Eucalyptus seedling count per one percentage point increase)

rows.note: Outcome: total Eucalyptus seedling count per 15x15 m quadrat visit, summed across all three height classes (euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m). Model: negative binomial (NB2) GLM with log link, fitted by maximum likelihood with the dispersion parameter alpha estimated jointly (alpha = 187.7, reflecting extreme overdispersion; three properties had zero seedlings, giving separated fixed effects that carry no recruitment information). Within-property dependence handled by property fixed effects (17 dummies for 18 properties); standard errors are model-based (not cluster-robust). Adjustments: Euc_canopy_cover, Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), Season (survey round). Native scale: log rate ratio per one percentage point of total grass cover; focal estimate = -0.00310 (95% CI -0.0213 to +0.0151), z = -0.333, p = 0.74, residual df = 325. Conclusion: no detectable effect of grass cover on Eucalyptus seedling recruitment; each additional percentage point of grass cover multiplies expected total seedling count by exp(-0.00310) = 0.997. Result stable across BFGS and Newton optimizers. Caution: alpha is large and the count distribution is zero-inflated, so power is limited. Observation unit: one quadrat in one survey round. Design: nested field survey, properties as spatial clusters, repeated rounds with non-overlapping quadrats.
rows.predictor: Total grass cover, in percentage points of the 15x15 m quadrat, computed as ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover; the focal estimate is the log rate ratio of total eucalypt seedling count per one percentage point increase in this sum.

Consistent with the earlier raw-scale fit (coef -0.004/pp, SE 0.009, also null). rows.note: Property fixed-effects Poisson GLM (log link) with HC1 heteroskedasticity-robust SEs. Adjusted for Euc_canopy_cover, Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m) (renamed dist_euc for formula parsing), and Season (3 rounds). Property entered as fixed effects (17 dummies), absorbing all property-attached covariates (climate, soil, management) and between-property dependence; HC1 SEs address overdispersion/heteroskedasticity. Exclusions: listwise deletion of missing model variables removed 3 of 351 rows (n=348); 3 all-zero-recruitment properties (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor) contribute nothing to the within-property likelihood under the log link, so the fitted n is 298 quadrat visits across 15 properties, df_resid=278. Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat sampled in one survey round (fresh random quadrats each round; quadrat labels not persistent). Result robust in direction to marginal alternatives (cluster-robust NB and Poisson, and exchangeable-correlation GEE) gave small negative marginal estimates, indicating earlier associations were driven by between-property contrasts; the within-property estimate reported here is the most conservative and least confounded quantity.
rows.predictor: Exotic grass cover, percent points: ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover

Conclusion: no detectable effect; point estimate slightly negative. Outcome construction: euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m. Focal estimate is on the model's native log(count+1) scale: +0.000912 per percentage point of native perennial grass cover (SE 0.003152, t = 0.289, residual df ~ 342, p ~ 0.77; exp(coef) = 1.00091) — an essentially null, slightly positive association. Property random-intercept variance 0.146 vs residual 0.599 confirms real between-property clustering. Robustness: alternative operationalizations of grass cover (all-grass sum and exotic-grass sum) under Poisson GEE fits with property-clustered robust SEs gave small non-significant negative coefficients (e.g. -0.0084, SE 0.0116); the log-linear mixed model gives a small non-significant positive coefficient — all support a null effect of grass cover on Eucalyptus seedling recruitment in these data.

rows.note: Focal model: negative binomial (NB2) GLM, MLE with property-clustered robust standard errors. Response: total Eucalyptus seedlings per 15x15 m quadrat-visit (sum of euc_sdlgs0_50cm + euc_sdlgs50cm_2m + euc_sdlgs>2m; verified identical to precomputed euc_sdlgs_all). Focal predictor: total grass cover in raw percentage points = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover; the coefficient is the log-rate ratio in expected seedling count per +1 percentage point of grass cover, signed so that negative = less recruitment with more grass. Nuisance structure: property fixed effects (18 dummies, absorbing all property-level confounding: soil, climate, seed-source context, management) + Season (survey round) factor. Missing data: the single row with missing grass-cover components (1 missing per grass column, same row) was handled by within-property median imputation rather than deletion; outcome counts and Season/Property were complete, so n = 351 of 351 rows. Estimate = -0.009110 (SE 0.011662, z = -0.781, p = 0.435; exp(beta) = 0.9909), i.e. about a 1% lower expected seedling count per extra percentage point of grass cover, not statistically distinguishable from zero. Overdispersion confirmed (seedling mean 1.85, variance 38.4; NB2 alpha = 5.55), justifying NB over Poisson. Caveat: three properties (Olive, Rokahr, Taylor) recorded essentially zero seedlings everywhere, so their fixed effects tend to -infinity (incidental zeros) and they contribute no within-property information to the grass coefficient; identification comes from within-property covariation. Observation unit: one quadrat sampled in one round; quadrats do not persist across rounds and quadrat labels are not persistent IDs. Design: nested survey, 18 properties (spatial clusters, used for FE and clustered SEs) x 3 rounds (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007), ~351 quadrat-visits total. Test statistic: z (large-sample Wald, cluster-robust); inferential reference: standard normal (df = 18 clusters inform the cluster-robust variance but the Wald test is asymptotic). An alternative defensible specification (adjusting for eucalypt canopy cover and season with listwise deletion instead of property FE) gave a nearly identical result (-0.0113, SE 0.0098), indicating the null-ish negative association is robust to confounding/missing-data handling.

Observation unit: one 15x15 m quadrat visit (quadrats not revisited across rounds). Estimate is on the native log-rate scale; larger values of the predictor mean more grass cover, so orientation is as_declared. Across alternative specifications (total grass cover, exotic grass cover, occurrence, size-weighted index) estimates ranged from -0.020 to +0.013 per pp, all statistically null at conventional thresholds.

rows.note: Model: logistic binomial GEE (population-averaged) with exchangeable within-property working correlation and robust (sandwich) covariance, clustered on Property (18 clusters). Outcome: binary occurrence of recruitment — presence of ≥1 Eucalyptus seedling in the 0–50 cm height class per 15×15 m quadrat visit (prevalence 11.7%). Focal predictor: total grass cover = ExoticAnnualGrass_cover + ExoticPerennialGrass_cover + NativePerennialGrass_cover (percentage points of quadrat ground cover); larger values = more grass, as_declared. Adjustment set: Euc_canopy_cover (%), Distance_to_Eucalypt_canopy(m), and Season (survey round, categorical). Missing data: property-median imputation for the few missing covariate values (1 grass/canopy cover value, 2 distances; outcome fully observed), so all 351 quadrat visits retained — no listwise deletion. Result: log-odds ratio per percentage point of grass cover = 0.00173 (SE 0.01103; z = 0.157, p ≈ 0.88; 95% CI −0.020 to +0.023; odds ratio per pp = 1.0017). Test statistic: Wald z = 0.157. Inferential df: 17 (clusters − 1). Fitted n = 351; observation unit = one 15×15 m quadrat in one survey round; design = nested cross-sectional survey, quadrats clustered within 18 properties, three seasonal rounds (Winter 2006, Spring 2006, Autumn 2007), physical quadrats not resampled across rounds. Conclusion: no detectable grass-cover effect on seedling-recruitment occurrence in the native log-odds scale; the interval excludes neither moderate negative nor moderate positive effects. Sensitivity: an earlier Poisson GEE on total seedling counts (before the outcome change) gave a similarly null, slightly negative estimate (−0.0084 log rate ratio per pp), and the listwise-deleted version of this logistic model was essentially identical (0.00162, SE 0.01108), so the result is stable across outcome construction and missing-data handling.
